scope: history integrity, transaction recovery, lineage, adapters, compatibility and native handoff

findings_sent_to_parent.finding: Project.init overwrites pre-existing main/scene.usda; initialization publishes config before scaffold completion.
Unvalidated captured_at becomes a directory path; bad/nested/date is reported committed but invisible to the history glob.
Parent and head selection uses captured_at sorting, so clock rollback creates wrong ancestry.
stage_path permits external entry_layer paths; verify can report ok for an unarchived external entry layer.
set_main can publish a new current.json while scene.usda remains the previous result; success event precedes publication.
Inbox publication before receipt lacks durable idempotency, allowing crash/retry duplicate commits.
A live service with a stale heartbeat is treated as stopped, and stop refuses to signal it during long import/RPC work.
Native Blender restoration uses a shared material revision as object identity and fails for two parts sharing a shader.
Rhino pending export queue is lost on hook reattachment or interpreter restart, stranding exact captured saves.
Cross-project adapter ownership is inconsistent: Blender retains old capture hooks; stopping old Rhino project removes the current hook; timed snapshots can steal ownership back.
findings_sent_to_parent.status: Fixed by this agent; parent service must call capture(..., respect_binding=True)

targeted_verification.native_probe_result: Blender 5.2.3 background process: two mesh objects share the same restored material; procedural native graph retains 4 nodes.

remaining_limitations: Rhino queue recovery requires an attached Rhino runtime to reopen the captured native staging documents. Failed captures are retained for explicit intervention rather than automatically retried forever.
Disposable annotated USD import projections are retained under .cadgit/staging; an interrupted handoff can leave cache/staging data for eventual cleanup.
Per-face/subset native material restoration remains unsupported and fails rather than inferring assignment.

Source identity is currently application-plus-branch, not an independently identified document stream. Different native files saved into one application branch share that history; document provenance is metadata.
Source histories and compatibility failures still require defensive indexing/quarantine if an unrelated committed manifest is malformed. One bad record can make broad history enumeration fail.
No general native geometry reconstruction, native full-document archive, or third-party plugin registry was added; these remain documented scope boundaries.
